niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces with strong, readable hierarchy; clear grouping into cards or sections; enough visible information to support comparison or decision-making; spacious spacing that reduces clutter; and polished visual depth through rounded corners, soft shadows, translucency, or layered panels. They frequently like dark navy or dark-themed UIs with high contrast and vivid but controlled accents, but in some contexts they also prefer light neutral surfaces when they improve readability and calmness. They generally favor layouts that feel organized, guided, and complete over sparse, ambiguous, or weakly structured screens.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers strong visual hierarchy with prominent titles or hero values, readable section labels, emphasized key actions, and an obvious scan path.
Prefers content organized into clearly separated cards, grouped sections, modular panels, or contained overlays rather than flat, floating, or weakly grouped layouts.
Usually prefers showing more useful information upfront—details, labels, metrics, options, or filled-out content states—when it improves clarity and comparison.
Prefers generous padding, breathing room, and cleaner compositions that avoid cramped stacking, overlapping controls, or excessive visual noise.
Prefers rounded cards, modals, and buttons with soft corners, though usually not the most exaggerated pill-heavy treatment unless it supports a friendly modal style.
Prefers subtle depth cues such as shadows, translucency, gradients, borders, and layered panels that create separation and a more polished interface.
Often prefers dark navy or dark-themed interfaces with strong contrast and vivid blue, purple, or cyan accents, especially when they feel immersive and clearly legible.
